title: Volcanic eruption
tldr: Follow the local volcano evacuation order and stay out of restricted zones. If ash is falling and you are not told to evacuate, stay indoors with windows and doors closed. Avoid river valleys where volcanic mudflows may travel.
steps: Use local emergency alerts and the responsible volcano observatory.
Take designated evacuation routes; do not approach the volcano to watch.
Close outside-air openings and use eye protection and a well-fitting particulate respirator for necessary outdoor movement.
Avoid driving in ash unless necessary; visibility and engines can be affected.
next: Wait for reentry instructions. Do not climb a roof covered in ash; wet ash can overload structures.
watch: A particle respirator does not protect against volcanic gases.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Keep away from river valleys, exclusion areas and visible ash plumes. Use the best reachable intact shelter for ashfall while checking evacuation information. Avoid driving through heavy ash unless leaving a more immediate threat; ash can impair engines and visibility.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
